entries.german:
Bischof Heinrich von Konstanz überträgt dem Kloster St. Katharinen St. Gallen Hof und Mühle zu Obersiebeneichen zu Zinseigen.

Wir a) Hainrich von gottes gnaden bischoff ze Costentz tůnt kvnt vnd bekennen offenlich mit disem gegenwúrtigen brief allen, die in ansehent alder ho erent lesen, daz fúr v´ns kam der ersam || vnser lieber getrúwer Hainrich der Wiener burger ze Costentz vnd offenot vor v´ns, daz in êhaht b) not von swarer gúlt wegen, dv´ vff in genauen wa er, darzůbraht vnd betwûngen het, daz er den hof vnd die || múli, dv´ vormals gewesen sint V olrichs in der Bv´nde des alten vogtes ze Costentz vnd siner sv´n, dv ze dem Obern Sibênaich gelegen sint, daz da stosset an daz Vnder Sibenâich, daz dez von Rosenberg vnd dez Rôten von || Wâtt ist, der selbe hoff vnd dv´ múli von v´ns vnd v´nserm gotzhus lehen ist, verkôffen mu esst, v^nd fv^nd aber nieman, der im als vil nûtzlicher barschaft darvmb geben wolt als die ersâmen in gât die gaischelichen ffrôwen des gotzhus ze sânt Katherinen in vnserm bistůme gelegen in der vorstat ze sant Gallen sant Agustines rêgel Predyer ordens. Vnd won die selben gaischelichen frôwen dez lehens nit geua ehig wa erint vnd och daz nit verdienen kvndin nach weltlichem rehten, als ain man von sins lehens wegen sinem herren billich diênen sol, do bat v´ns der selb Hainrich der Wiener demu eteklich, daz wir den selben gaischelichen ffrowen den obgenanten hof ze dem Obern Sibenaich vnd die múli mit aller iro zůgeho ervng zů ir vnd ir gotzhus handen luterlich durch got bringen weltin vnd inen si aigenen wo eltin, so wolte aber er dafúr vmbetwungenlich vnd och da wider v´ns an v´nser hant willeclich vff geben die aigenschaft sins huses vnd der hofstat, dv´ ze Costentz in der stat an sant Pawlus gassen 1 an der stetringmúr zwischen dez Ffryen, der Betmingerinen vnd dez Segers húsern vnd hofraitinen gelegen sint, vnd wolte och daz selb hus eweclich von v´ns vnd von v´nserm gotzhus ze rehtem lehen haben vnd vollefu ert och daz an vnser hant, als reht was. Darv´ber so woltent och die obgenanten gaischelichen frowen v´ns vnd v´nseren nachkomen jemêr mêr êweclich ainen vierdvng wahs in vnser vnd in ains bischofs kamer, wer danne jemer herre ze Costenz ist, von dem obgenanten hof ze Sibenaich vnd der múli geben ja ergelichs je vff v´nser ffrowen tag ze der liehtmisse. Da haben wir bedaht vnd angesehen, daz der appostel der hailig zwelfbotte Pawlus schribet, wer sin gůte milteklich durch got git, darvmb daz sin nam vnd sin lob vff ertrich gelobt vnd geêret werde, daz dv´ tûgent ander tugent fúrtreffent sie. Vnd darvmb wie daz ist, daz die obgenanten gaischelichen ffrôwen daz selbe lehen des hôues vnd der múli ze Sibenach nit verdienen kv´nnent nach welchem c) rehten, so zwifelent wir daran nit, daz si es gen got verdiênen wellint mit singen mit lesen mit ir anda ehtigem gebêtte vnd mit anderen gůten werken, die si v ebent sint. Vnd darvmb so haben och wir mit gůtem willen vmbetwungenlich vnd mit gůter vorbetrahtv^nge mit der erwirdigen vnser lieben anda ehtigen getrûwen dez tegans vnd dez cappittels der korherren der stift v´nser ffrôwen ze dem thůme ze Costentz willen vnd gûnst den obgenanten hof vnd die múli mit aller ir zůgeho erde ffrilich vnd willeclich von svndern gnaden mit rehter wissent lûterlich durh got, dem si dienstlich verpflîhtet sint, vffgeben der pryorinen des obgenanten gotzhus ze sant Katherinen an des selben conuentes vnd gotzhus stat vnd gebent inen vnd dem selben irem gotzhus den selben hof vnd múli mit allen nútzen vnd zůgeho erden ze ainem rehten zinsaigen mit disem brief, also daz der selbe hof ze dem Obern Sibenaich vnd och dv´ selbe múli vnd waz darzů ho ert nv^ hinnanhin jemer mêr eweclich iren b) vnd iren nachkomen vnd dem selben irem gotzhus ze ainem rehten zinsaigen vmb ain vierdvng wahs beliben sol. Vnd haben v´ns och darv´ber mit der obgenanten herrên ze dem thůme willen vnd gvnst fúr vns vnd alle v´nser nachkomen gen der selben . . pryorinen vnd gen dem cônuente gemainlich dez gotzhus ze sant Katherinen vnd gen dem selben irem gotzhus ffrilich vnd offenlich verzigen des obgenanten hôues vnd der múli vnd daran aller aigenschaft aller lehenschaft aller vorderv^ng aller ansprâch vnd alles dienstliches rehten, so v´ns von dem selben hof volgen solt, vnd aller ander reht, so wir an dem selben hof vnd der múli v^ntz her gehebt haben ald nv^ ald hernach von dekainen dingen jemer daran gewinnen mo ehtin von dekainer slaht geriht alder reht gaischelichs ald weltlichs, doch alleweg svnderlich mit so elichen rehten vnd mit der beschaidenhait, daz die selben gaischlichen frôwen vnd och alle ir nachkomen vns vnd och allen v´nseren nachkomen bischoff ze Costentz nv^ hinnanhin jemer mêr êweclich a ellv´ jar besvnder in ains bischoffs kâmer geben sont jê ze vnser ffrowen tag ze der liehtmisse ainen vierdvng wahse von dez selben zinsaigens wêgen, doch mit so elichen rehten, ob der selb zins der vierdvng wâhs nv^ ald hernâch dekaines jars versessen wûrde vnd nit geriht oder gegeben wûrde ze dem zil, als vor ist beschaiden, ez wa er v´nser oder ir halb von hinla essi von vergessens ald von ander sach wêgen, wie sich daz fûgti, wênne vnd wie dik oder wie offt daz bescha ehe, darvmb haben wir noch vnser nachkomen noch niêman andre von vnseren noch von vnser gotzhus wegen doch nit anders rehtes ze dem selben gotzhus noch ze dem selben gaischelichen vnd ze dem obgenanten hof vnd ze der múli ze Sibenaich vnd was darzů ho ert nit anders ze sprêchent, won das v´nser amptlúte alle verssessen zins mit dem rehten wol erlangen múgent, ob si went, vngeuârlich. Vnd ist och dis alles mit v´nser hantgetât willen vnd gvnst âne geuerde beschehen vnd vollefu ert mit allen den worten werken vnd och geta eten vnd mit aller kraft, so darzů hôrt vnd nôtdúrftig was nach gewônhait vnd nach reht. Vnd ze warem vnd offeme vrkv´nde vnd sta eter jêmer werender ewiger sicherhait aller dirre vorgeschriben dinge haben wir vorbenenter bischoff Hainrich v´nser insigel gehenket an disen brief. Darnach vergehint wir . . der tegan vnd daz cappittel gemainlich ze dem thůme ze Costentz, daz wir och dez selben vnsers cappittels insigel gehenket an disen brief, won och dis vorgeschriben alles mit v´nserm willen vollefu ert ist, als vor ist beschaiden. Der brief ist ze Costêntz geben, do man von Cristes gebúrt zalte drv´zehenhvndert jar, darnach in dem sehs vnd sibentzigosten jar, an sant Verênen abende.

entries.english:
Bishop Heinrich of Konstanz transfers to the convent of St. Katharina in St. Gallen the farm and mill at Obersiebeneichen as rent-bearing property.

We, Heinrich, by the grace of God bishop of Konstanz, make known and openly declare by this present letter to all who see, hear, or read it: The honorable and dear faithful Heinrich the Wiener, citizen of Konstanz, came before us and explained that severe debt, which pressed heavily upon him, had compelled him to sell the farm and mill at Obersiebeneichen. They had formerly belonged to Ulrich in der Bünde, the old bailiff of Konstanz, and his son; they lie at Ober-Siebeneichen, adjoining Unter-Siebeneichen, which belongs to the von Rosenberg and the Rôten von Wâtt. The farm and mill are fiefs held from us and our church. He could find no one willing to pay him as much useful cash for them as the honorable, devout women of the convent of St. Katharina in our diocese, in the suburb of St. Gallen, of the Order of Preachers of the Rule of St. Augustine.

Since these devout women were not eligible to hold the fief and could not render the service required by secular law of a man for his fief, Heinrich the Wiener humbly asked us to transfer the above-mentioned farm at Ober-Siebeneichen and the mill, with all their appurtenances, purely for God's sake into the hands of those women and their convent, and to make them its owners. In return, he wished, freely and without compulsion, to surrender to us and our church the ownership of his house and its plot, located in the city of Konstanz on St. Paul's Street, by the town wall, between the houses and courtyards of the Ffrye, the Betmingerin, and the Seger. He wished to hold that same house from us and our church forever as a proper fief, and duly completed this exchange into our hands as required by law.

Moreover, the aforesaid devout women wished to give us and our successors, forever and in perpetuity, one vierdung of wax each year from the aforesaid farm at Siebeneichen and the mill, for our chamber and that of whichever bishop is then lord at Konstanz, payable on each feast of Our Lady of Candlemas.

We considered and reflected that the holy apostle Paul writes that whoever gives generously for God's sake, so that his name and praise may be celebrated and honored on earth, thereby excels in virtue. Therefore, although the aforesaid devout women cannot render the service due under secular law for the fief of the farm and mill at Siebeneichen, we have no doubt that they will render it to God through singing, reading, their devout prayers, and the other good works they perform.

Accordingly, with the consent and approval of our venerable, dear, devout, and faithful dean and chapter of canons of the cathedral church of Our Lady at Konstanz, and after good and careful consideration, we have freely and without compulsion, by special grace and with full knowledge, purely for God's sake—to whose service they are devoted—surrendered the aforesaid farm and mill, with all their appurtenances, to the prioress of the aforesaid convent of St. Katharina on behalf of that convent and house of religion. By this letter, we grant to the prioress and her convent the same farm and mill, with all their revenues and appurtenances, as proper rent-bearing property, on condition that the farm at Ober-Siebeneichen, the mill, and whatever belongs to them now or henceforth shall remain forever in perpetuity with the prioress, her successors, and their convent as proper rent-bearing property in return for one vierdung of wax.

With the consent and approval of the aforesaid lords of the cathedral, on behalf of ourselves and all our successors, we have also freely and publicly renounced, in favor of the prioress, the convent collectively, and their house of St. Katharina, all ownership, feudal rights, claims, demands, and service rights in the aforesaid house and mill, as well as every other right that we have hitherto held in them or might ever acquire in the future by any means, under any ecclesiastical or secular jurisdiction or law. This renunciation is subject, however, to the specific condition that those devout women and all their successors shall forever give to us and all our successors as bishops of Konstanz, each year without exception and separately into a bishop's chamber, one vierdung of wax from this rent-bearing property on the feast of Our Lady of Candlemas.

If that rent of one vierdung of wax should at any time, now or in the future, fall into arrears and not be paid at the appointed time, whether through negligence on our part or theirs, forgetfulness, or any other cause, however and as often as this might happen, neither we nor our successors nor anyone else on behalf of us or our church shall thereby acquire any further right to the convent, the devout women, the aforesaid farm and mill at Siebeneichen, or anything belonging to them. Our officials may, without prejudice, recover any arrears by lawful means if they wish.

All this was done and duly completed with our own consent and approval, in good faith, with all the words, acts, and deeds and with all the force required, as custom and law demanded. As true and open testimony and lasting, perpetual security for all the matters written above, we, the aforesaid Bishop Heinrich, have attached our seal to this letter. We, the dean and chapter collectively of the cathedral church at Konstanz, also declare that we have attached our chapter seal to this letter, since all the foregoing was duly completed with our consent, as stated above.

The letter was given at Konstanz in the year 1376 after the birth of Christ, on the eve of St. Verena's feast day [August 31].

Seals: two seals, the first damaged, like the first seal in No. 4606; the second slightly damaged, like the seal in No. 1282. — On the upper right of the reverse: traces of the vicar general's red seal ring.
